items.title: Handling User Input and Connecting Widgets to Functions

source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic Handling User Input and Connecting Widgets to Functions as printed (PDF 55-56, printed 51-52); its own lesson since 2026-10-29 (one lesson per book heading), moved from the topic 4.1 lesson.

blocks.text: User input is given through widgets like entry fields and buttons. Widgets are connected to functions in the program. When the widget is used, the connected function executes. This allows the program to process the input. For example, a button click can display a message. Proper connections ensure correct program behavior. This interaction improves user experience.

A simple login form allows a user to enter a username and password. Entry fields are used to take the input from the user. A button is provided to submit the information. When the button is clicked, the program checks the entered data. A message is then shown for success or error.

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import messagebox

# Create main window
window = tk.Tk()
window.title("Login Form")
window.geometry("300x200")

# Function to check login
def check_login():
    username = entry_user.get()
    password = entry_pass.get()

    # simple check
    if username == "admin" and password == "1234":
        messagebox.showinfo("Success", "Login Successful!")
    else:
        messagebox.showerror("Error", "Invalid Username or Password")

# Username label and entry
tk.Label(window, text="Username").pack()
entry_user = tk.Entry(window)
entry_user.pack()

# Password label and entry
tk.Label(window, text="Password").pack()
entry_pass = tk.Entry(window, show="*")
entry_pass.pack()

# Login button
tk.Button(window, text="Login", command=check_login).pack(pady=10)

# Run application
window.mainloop()
